paragraphs.title: Praise, Gratitude, and Faith Through Every Season

answers: To give thanks unto the LORD
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “It is a good thing to give thanks unto the LORD.”
easy.q: What is described as a good thing?

easy.explanation: The psalm calls God’s people to sing praises unto His name.
Verse 2 says, “To shew forth thy lovingkindness in the morning.”
easy.q: When is the LORD’s lovingkindness shown forth?

medium.explanation: The verse says to show forth His faithfulness “every night.”
medium.q: When is the LORD’s faithfulness declared?

answers: An instrument of ten strings, the psaltery, and the harp
medium.explanation: Verse 3 names an instrument of ten strings, the psaltery, and the harp.
medium.q: What instruments are mentioned in these verses?

answers: Because of the works of God’s hands
Because he has gained great wealth
medium.explanation: He says, “I will triumph in the works of thy hands.”
medium.q: Why does the psalmist say he will triumph?

answers: Praise is offered continually, in the morning and at night
Praise is offered only during battles
Praise is offered only by musicians
challenge.explanation: The passage joins morning testimony, nightly faithfulness, and musical praise.
challenge.q: What pattern of worship is presented in the passage?

answers: They are presented as two ways to praise God
Thanksgiving is directed toward human rulers
challenge.explanation: The verse places giving thanks and singing praises together as acts of worship.
challenge.q: How are thanksgiving and singing related in verse 1?

answers: God’s works give him reason to rejoice
God’s works are hidden from everyone
challenge.explanation: The psalmist says that the LORD has made him glad through His work.
challenge.q: What does the psalmist’s gladness reveal about God’s works?

paragraphs.title: The Depth of God’s Works and the Fate of the Wicked

easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “O LORD, how great are thy works!”
easy.q: How does the psalmist describe the LORD’s works?

easy.explanation: The fool does not understand the greatness of God’s works and thoughts.
easy.q: What does the fool fail to understand?

answers: They shall be destroyed for ever
They shall become righteous by their own power
easy.explanation: The passage says that the wicked shall be destroyed for ever.
easy.q: What happens to the wicked in the end?

medium.explanation: Verse 5 declares, “thy thoughts are very deep.”
medium.q: How are the LORD’s thoughts described?

medium.explanation: Verse 7 says, “When the wicked spring as the grass.”
medium.q: What are the wicked compared to when they flourish?

answers: They are planted in God’s house
medium.explanation: Verse 9 says, “all the workers of iniquity shall be scattered.”
medium.q: What happens to the workers of iniquity?

answers: God’s deep wisdom is contrasted with the fool’s lack of understanding
The harp is contrasted with the trumpet
challenge.explanation: The psalm contrasts the depth of God’s thoughts with the fool’s inability to understand.
challenge.q: What contrast is emphasized in this section?

answers: Their success is temporary and cannot prevent judgment
They are firmly planted in righteousness
challenge.explanation: The comparison to grass emphasizes their brief and passing flourishing.
challenge.q: What does the image of grass suggest about the flourishing of the wicked?

answers: He is most high for evermore
He is uncertain about their future
challenge.explanation: The LORD remains most high for evermore while His enemies perish and evil workers are scattered.
challenge.q: How is the LORD’s position described in relation to the fate of the wicked?

paragraphs.title: The Righteous Are Raised and Their Enemies Fall

easy.explanation: He says, “my horn shalt thou exalt.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist say will happen to his horn?

easy.explanation: Verse 10 says, “I shall be anointed with fresh oil.”
easy.q: With what shall the psalmist be anointed?

answers: The downfall of their enemies and the wicked
easy.explanation: The psalmist says his eyes shall see and his ears shall hear concerning those who rise against him.
easy.q: What will the righteous be able to see and hear?

medium.explanation: Fresh oil can signify renewal, strength, or anointing.
medium.q: What may fresh oil suggest in this passage?

medium.explanation: He speaks of what his eye shall see and what his ears shall hear.
medium.q: What does the psalmist use to describe his experience of deliverance?

answers: The priests in the house of God
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to wicked enemies who oppose the psalmist.
medium.q: Who are those that rise up against the psalmist?

answers: The psalmist is lifted up while his enemies are brought down
Both the psalmist and his enemies are exalted
challenge.explanation: The passage presents the righteous person’s elevation alongside the enemies’ defeat.
challenge.q: What relationship appears between the exaltation of the psalmist and the enemies’ fate?

challenge.explanation: The exalted horn is a biblical image of strength and honor.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “my horn” most likely represent here?

answers: God gives strength and vindication to the righteous
Worship is limited to the night
challenge.explanation: The verses describe God strengthening the psalmist and giving him victory over his enemies.
challenge.q: What central idea unites these two verses?

paragraphs.title: The Flourishing of the Righteous and the Endurance of Goodness

answers: A palm tree and a cedar
easy.explanation: Verse 12 says, “The righteous shall flourish like the palm tree: he shall grow like a cedar in Lebanon.”
easy.q: What is the righteous person compared to?

answers: In the house of the LORD
In the camp of the wicked
easy.explanation: Verse 13 says they are “planted in the house of the LORD.”
Verse 14 says, “They shall still bring forth fruit in old age.”
easy.q: What will the righteous do in old age?

answers: A lasting source of spiritual flourishing
medium.explanation: Those planted in the LORD’s house continue to flourish in His courts.
medium.q: What does being planted in the house of the LORD imply?

medium.explanation: The verse says they shall be “fat and flourishing.”
medium.q: How are the righteous described in their later years?

medium.explanation: Verse 15 says their lives show that the LORD is upright.
medium.q: What does the life of the righteous show about the LORD?

challenge.explanation: The trees picture the strength, stability, and flourishing of the righteous.
challenge.q: What do the palm tree and cedar symbolize in this passage?

answers: Faithful goodness can continue throughout life
Only young people can serve God
challenge.explanation: The phrase teaches that fruitfulness and service can continue even in old age.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the phrase “still bring forth fruit in old age”?

answers: The LORD is upright and has no unrighteousness in Him
The righteous prosper because of their own power
The wicked are the true examples of faithfulness
challenge.explanation: The final verse declares, “the LORD is upright: he is my rock, and there is no unrighteousness in him.”
challenge.q: How does the final verse summarize the section?
